requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale: The bundled bootstrap skill maps every first-party test to a requirement or example and maps user-visible source units to requirements. Cargo metadata distributes the skill from assets/skills, and the getting-started guide directs users to it.

text: description: Build an initial Habeas requirement set from an existing codebase by tracing its tests and user-visible behavior; use for requirements bootstrapping or coverage audits.

Read the project's existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests before writing new requirements. Follow behavior through the code rather than relying only on test names or top-level dispatch.
- Every first-party runnable test or test case, including integration tests, doctests, and parameterized cases where present. Record the requirement or example IDs each test checks.

- Every first-party source unit that appears to implement end-user-visible functionality or interactions. Record file locations and requirement IDs for relevant public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches. Do not count one tagged entry point as coverage for deeper user-visible code.
Exclude generated and third-party code from the inventories. If a candidate looks user-facing but its purpose is unclear, keep it on the gap list until resolved.

Treat requirements inferred from existing code as proposals. Show the user their proposed full IDs and exact text, along with uncertainty about whether observed behavior is intended or a bug. Obtain agreement on the proposals before installing them in the mdBook; prior explicit agreement to the same requirements counts.

Create or reuse the agreed, stable, chapter-qualified `{req}` requirements in the mdBook. State observable obligations with BCP 14 terms. Group tests that check the same behavior under one requirement; several tests MAY share an ID. For tests of internal invariants, write a requirement for the invariant they actually check rather than inventing a user-facing promise. Distinguish intended behavior from a possible bug or incidental implementation detail.

Put at least one `{test}` reference with a full requirement or example name on each test definition or individual case. A parameterized test can carry a reference at its case source or generating declaration when that is the only editable source. Add multiple references when a test checks multiple definitions. Do not use one file-level tag to stand in for unrelated tests.

Map each inventoried user-visible source unit to a requirement and add `{impl}` references at meaningful implementation points, including distinct observable branches. Do not tag every line. Use the bundled `habeas-requirements` and `habeas-evidence` guidance for directive syntax and evidence records. Each evidence record must cite exact current lines covering every reference to its definition. Judge the requirement or example from the code and test results; a tag alone does not justify `determination: true`.

Run the project tests and Habeas validation, then review both inventories independently: Habeas checks references that exist but does not detect an untagged test or omitted user-visible code. Report test-tag coverage and user-visible implementation coverage as mapped counts over total counts. Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items. List remaining gaps with file locations and reasons; do not invent evidence or silently exclude difficult cases.

Use the `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill to derive an initial set of requirements from an existing codebase and its tests. Setup does not write requirements or evidence for you. See [How it works](./reference.md) for those steps, the evidence index, and instructions for using a local checkout.
